text:
cassandra_support: ACME reporting big p95/p99 spike since 08:10 UTC, p99 ~2.3s (normally ~120ms). Also seeing some 503s and auth timeouts on their tenant. Investigating now.
priya_sre_oncall: thanks, what's the tenant id and any correlating infra alerts? :eyes:
cassandra_support: tenant acme-inc-42, alerting showed GPU OOM signals on several serving pods + repeated slab compaction messages. Logs show KV cache growth for that tenant (per-tenant kv_bytes).
jon_eng_runtime: can you paste the OOM lines and the kv metrics snapshot?
cassandra_support: pasted snippets below:```
[2026-03-16T08:09:58Z] runtime[pid=2234]: GPU OOM signal received on device 0, evicting slabs
[2026-03-16T08:10:01Z] runtime[pid=2234]: kv_cache: tenant=acme-inc-42 bytes=4.2G entries=128k
[2026-03-16T08:10:02Z] runtime[pid=2234]: slab_compact: reclaimed=12MB free=24MB
[2026-03-16T08:10:05Z] auth[pid=1190]: token-verify timeout=1200ms upstream=redis auth-cache-miss
```
cassandra_support: also hitting 503s when requests hit slower paths.
marco_infra: rolling up infra view: GPU mem used on cluster-gpu-1 jumped from 60%->95% at 08:09. Several pods on node gpu-3 show OOM events. Node-level logs show repeated page faults and vmalloc warns.
emily_allocator: allocator note: we've seen this pattern when per-tenant KV grows without eviction pressure — the slab allocator fragments and fails to find contiguous chunks for large KV entries leading to GPU OOMs even though aggregate free memory exists.
priya_sre_oncall: ok immediate mitigations? Can we route new requests for acme to fallback capacity / smaller model?
jon_eng_runtime: yes we can flip tenant routing: set a routing override to `fallback:small-v2` for acme-inc-42, or enable active-fallback-tier, that will lower memory usage. Also can reduce max_batch_size for that tenant.
nina_support_lead: tell ACME we're routing them to fallback and working on permanent fix, thanks.
priya_sre_oncall: commands to check current state for oncall:```
kubectl -n runtime get pods -l tenant=acme-inc-42 -o wide
kubectl -n runtime logs <pod> -c runtime | grep -E "OOM|slab_compact|kv_cache"
rdctl routing get --tenant acme-inc-42
```
jon_eng_runtime: repro steps for devs: run a tuned script that simulates many small requests that increase KV working set:```bash
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_TOKEN" -d '{"input":"short"}' https://api.redwood.local/v1/generate >/dev/null &
done
sleep 30
rdctl metrics snapshot --tenant acme-inc-42 | grep kv_cache
```
emily_allocator: short-term fixes we can apply now: 1) enable more aggressive slab compaction (set slab.compact_threshold=0.25) 2) temporarily reduce per-tenant kv_max_bytes to 1GB for acme 3) restart runtime workers on node gpu-3 sequentially to trigger fresh arenas.
marco_infra: I'll take the sequential restarts and set node-level thermostat to prefer eviction: kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-worker -n runtime --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-3 --timeout=120s (do one pod at a time).
priya_sre_oncall: emily, can you confirm the allocator knobs and safe ranges? We don't want a regression in throughput.
emily_allocator: safe ranges: slab.compact_threshold from default 0.5 -> 0.25 is low risk for short window. kv_max_bytes override per-tenant: 1GB should be fine, will increase tail p99 slightly but prevents OOM. We'll monitor p95/p99.
jon_eng_runtime: also recommend enabling active-cache-eviction-policy: lru_ttl=300s for that tenant. That will trim stale prefixes.
cassandra_support: applied routing override to fallback model and informed customer. They see immediate latency improvement but a few requests still 5xx as recycled workers come up. :relieved:
deploy_bot: deployment/runtime-worker rollout started for node=gpu-3 by marco_infra at 08:18 UTC :rocket:
marco_infra: one pod restarted, mem pressure dropped on gpu-3 from 95% -> 78%. Continuing sequential restarts.
priya_sre_oncall: good. after rollout completes can we snapshot metrics and compare p95/p99?
jon_eng_runtime: yes will collect:```
rdctl metrics timeseries --tenant acme-inc-42 --window=30m --series=p95_latency,p99_latency,kb_gpu_mem,kv_bytes > /tmp/acme-snapshot-08-20.log
```
emily_allocator: follow-up medium-term: we should add per-tenant KV quotas + early backpressure. i'll open a ticket to implement conservative defaults and a circuit-breaker that returns 429 before slab fragmentation cascades.
nina_support_lead: please keep me posted, i'll send ACME a short incident note and expected ETA for full remediation.
priya_sre_oncall: current plan summary: 1) route acme to small-v2 fallback (done) 2) set kv_max_bytes=1GB for acme (in flight) 3) enable aggressive slab compaction for 30m window (in flight) 4) sequential restart of affected pods (marco done ongoing) 5) collect metrics and re-evaluate at 08:45 UTC.
cassandra_support: ACME confirmed reduction in errors and p99 down to ~350ms after routing override. I'll keep monitoring and escalate if they see anything else.
emily_allocator: assigning follow-ups: EMILY -> ticket allocator#2345 for per-tenant quotas; JON -> add eviction telemetry to console; MARCO -> node restart summary; PRIYA -> incident postmortem draft.
priya_sre_oncall: thanks team. If anything spikes again, tag me and we'll roll back routing. :thumbsup:
